classification.difficultyReason: Use the marked equal half-base lengths to identify a right triangle, then calculate an irrational shorter side.

content.prompt:
Triangle $ABC$ is equilateral, with each side of length $2\text{ cm}$. Find the length of $BX$.

Use the square-root table on printed page 206 to give an approximation correct to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Equilateral triangle ABC, with B above midpoint X of AC. All three outer sides retain their 2 cm labels. Equal-length ticks mark AX and XC; a right-angle square marks BX perpendicular to AC. Ordinary source-blue outlines become house black; the meaningful red dashed altitude is retained.
spec.mathematics: AB=BC=AC=2 cm; AX=XC; BX is perpendicular to AC.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied measurements, point names and geometric marks are visible.

answer.worked:
The matching ticks show that $AX=XC$, so $AX=1\text{ cm}$. In right-angled triangle $ABX$, Pythagoras’ theorem gives:
$$\begin{align*}BX^2+1^2&=2^2\\BX^2+1&=4\\BX^2&=4-1\\BX^2&=3\\BX&=\sqrt{3}\end{align*}$$
Using the square-root table on printed page 206, $BX\approx1.73\text{ cm}$, correct to 2 decimal places.
